gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the BLUETTI Apex 300 takes solar through only two XT60 ports rated 12–60 V and 20 A each. The 500 W panels in BLUETTI's own $3,299 Apex 300 + 2 × 500W bundle are each 49.1 V Voc, so they have to go one per port and cannot be wired in series (2 × 49.1 = 98.2 V). The $699 SolarX 4K that raises solar input to about 4 kW accepts only 150–500 V strings.
standout_why: I compared against ChatGPT's results: the ankersolix.com F3800 / F3800 Plus pages (results 1–3), the Jackery 5000 Plus manual and product pages (4, 5, 7, 8, 11–17), and the Anker F3800 Plus Technical Brief (6, 9, 10; the PDF would not render as text for me). None of them covers BLUETTI or the Apex 300, so none gives its 12–60 V XT60 solar limit, the one-panel-per-port rule for 49.1 V panels, or the 150–500 V floor on the SolarX 4K. The main Anker trap is already on rival result 1: ankersolix.com/products/f3800?skimoffer=3789496 now serves the F3800 Plus page, which says '(Note: The 240V output cannot be used while the device is charging via 120V AC.)' That would only score 1 for Anker. This finding is new and useful but describes how to wire the kit rather than which kit to buy, so 2 and not 3.
kit_items: Power station with 240 V from one unit: BLUETTI Apex 300 (2,764.8 Wh, 3,840 W, NEMA 14-50R at 120/240 V, switched by a voltage selector per StorageReview). It is already listed (bluetti-apex-300), it is on an approved store (awin:bluetti_us), and BLUETTI's page says it runs 120 V and 240 V loads 'even while charging'. Anker's page says the F3800 Plus cannot use its 240 V output while charging on 120 V AC.

Solar panels: 2 × BLUETTI SORA 500 (49.1 V Voc, 13.31 A Isc per Impulse Gamer). Put one panel in each of the Apex 300's two XT60 inputs (12–60 V, max 20 A). Never wire the two in series into one port: 98.2 V is over the 60 V limit. 13.31 A Isc is under the 20 A port limit.

Panel-to-station cable: MC4 to XT60 rated 20 A (BLUETTI 'Solar Charging Cable (20A MC4 to XT60)', $29). The Apex 300 box has no solar cable. BLUETTI also sells a 10 A MC4-to-XT60 cable, which is below the SORA 500's 13.31 A Isc, so the 20 A one is the right buy if the panel box lacks a cable.

Do not add: SolarX 4K ($699). It accepts only 150–500 V panel strings, which means at least four SORA 500s in series (3 × 49.1 = 147.3 V is still under 150 V), so it does nothing for a two-panel portable kit.
